AirTag 2 is launching this year, with improvements in tracking range and speaker volume. However, one important feature has not been improved: battery life. Fortunately, there's an accessory that can extend the AirTag 2's battery life from about one year to 10 years or more.

AirTag accessory extends battery life to 10 years or longer

Among Apple's many battery-powered products, there's one popular product that doesn't let you charge it: the AirTag.

The original AirTag has always been this way, and the AirTag 2 also requires a battery replacement about once a year.

The AirTag 2's battery life is the same as the previous generation. But there's a third-party accessory that I've personally used and can highly recommend, which can significantly extend battery life from 1 year to 10 years or even longer.

Elevation Lab's AirTag extended battery case essentially turns your AirTag into an 'AirTag Max.'

You place an AirTag 1 or 2 into the battery case (both models are compatible), then add two AA batteries, and the AirTag's battery capacity increases 14 times.

This design is quite clever and works very well. The only downside is that the case makes the AirTag bulkier. But I've found that many times you don't need the AirTag to be that small, so the case's size really isn't an issue.

You can order the AirTag battery kit on Amazon in several configurations:

Elevation Lab also makes a more compact version with 5 years of battery life instead of 10. So if the 10-year version is too bulky for you, there's another option to consider.

The AirTag's one-year battery life is actually not bad. But if you have a bunch of AirTags tracking different items, constantly getting low battery notifications can be annoying. If you don't mind the extra bulk of the case, I highly recommend Elevation Lab's solution.
